paper_sections.title: Neural Correlates of Social Inclusion in Borderline Personality Disorder
Interaction effect of group and ball tossing condition

description.value: The study examined neural responses to social inclusion, exclusion, and passive watching during a cyberball fMRI paradigm in females with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and healthy controls, and related BPD neural alterations to psychopathological features.

design.value: A between-group, within-subject block-design fMRI study using a 3 × 3 model with group (HC, BPD, MD) and condition (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion).

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV [SCID-I and -II]

description.value: Clinical diagnoses of MD and BPD were verified using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV.
BPD symptom severity was assessed by the Borderline Symptom List; total scores were divided by the number of items.
Current depressive symptoms were assessed using the Beck Depression Inventory, second edition, in its German version.
A self-reporting questionnaire containing 30 items rated on a 4-point Likert scale was used to assess impulsivity as a personality trait; higher sum scores reflect higher trait impulsivity.

Trait rejection sensitivity was assessed with a German version of the Rejection Sensitivity Questionnaire. Total scores were calculated by multiplying scores from the anxiety or concern subscale with inverted scores of the expectancy of acceptance subscale and dividing by the number of items.

The scale consists of eight questions concerning sensitivity in social situations, with each question rated on a 5-point Likert scale; higher total scores correspond to higher sensitivity to social exclusion.

The established 20-item Need-Threat-Scale assessed distress after social exclusion. It comprises four subscales—feeling excluded, low self-worth, meaningless existence, and control—with five items each. Items were rated from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very much), and total scores were divided by 20.

After the fMRI-scanning, subjective emotional experience was assessed for angry, sad, happy, afraid, frustrated, satisfied, helpless, and inner tension on a visual rating scale from 1 (very low) to 4 (very strong).
Handedness was assessed according to the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory.

task_description.value: Participants took part in a virtual ball-tossing game with two other participants who were supposed to be in another room. In fact, participants played against the computer and all actions were pre-programmed. Participants were represented by a hand at the bottom part of a screen, while the other players were represented by animated comic figures.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to take part in the virtual ball-tossing game; during passive watching they were asked just to watch the game and the computer controlled their character.

stimuli.value: A virtual ball-tossing game with two animated comic figures and the participant represented by a hand at the bottom part of a screen.

description.value: A T2*-sensitive gradient echo sequence was used for functional imaging with an echo time of 33 ms, flip angle of 90°, field of view of 230 mm, slice thickness of 2.5 mm with an interslice gap of 0.5 mm, and repetition time of 2,000 ms. Thirty-five transversal slices were recorded with an image size of 64 × 64 pixels during the cyberball task. This acquisition was used for the HC- and BPD-groups.

instrument.value: 3T MAGNETOM Allegra and 3T MAGNETOM Prisma Scanner (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: Anatomical high-resolution T1-weighted images were acquired for reasons of coregistration and normalization into standardized stereotactic space.

Data from each session were pre-processed including slice-timing, realignment, and normalization into a standard template (Montreal Neurological Institute, MNI) with a spatial resolution of 2 × 2 × 2 mm3. Smoothing was applied with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel.

software.value: Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM12, Wellcome Department, London, United Kingdom)

model_settings.value: The cyberball task was modeled as three separate blocks of condition (passive watching, inclusion and exclusion). Regressors representing the six motion parameters were integrated into the design matrix. Intrinsic autocorrelations were accounted for by AR(1), and low frequency drifts were removed via high-pass filtering (1/128s). Beta-images representing the averaged, estimated magnitude of neural activation associated with passive watching, inclusion, and exclusion were computed for each participant.

For second level group analyses, a 3 × 3 ANOVA model (omnibus F-test) was computed with the two factors group (HC, BPD, MD) and condition (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion), including first level contrasts for the three ball tossing conditions for each group. Scanner type and age were included as covariates in further analyses. Group-by-condition interaction effects were inferred at p < 0.001 at the voxel-level with at least 90 contiguously significant voxels corresponding to FWE correction of p < 0.05 on cluster level. Single tailed t-interaction contrasts were computed for significant main effects.

Correlation analyses were computed between significant differential cluster fMRI parameter estimates and scores from psychometric scales that differed significantly between BPD and both control groups, specifically BSL- and RSQ-scores, within BPD patients.

description.value: Participants were asked just to watch the game and the computer controlled their character.
Participants had random ball possession in one third of tosses.
The session started with 10 throws of 30% randomized ball possession and then participants were excluded from the game for the remaining 50 throws.

definition.value: A 3 × 3 ANOVA model with the two factors group (HC, BPD, MD) and condition (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion), with group-by-condition interaction effects examined for differential social inclusion versus passive watching neural activation.

interpretations.value: Significant group-by-condition interaction effects were observed within the dorsolateral and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, temporoparietal junction, posterior cingulate cortex and precuneus.

definition.value: Post-hoc single tailed t-interaction contrast comparing differential (social inclusion vs. passive watching) neural activations between BPD and HC.

interpretations.value: Enhanced neural activities within the dmPFC (BA9), the TPJ (BA22), and the PCC (BA23) in BPD compared to HC under social inclusion vs. passive watching conditions.

definition.value: Post-hoc single tailed t-interaction contrast comparing differential (social inclusion vs. passive watching) neural activations between BPD and MD.

interpretations.value: Differential (social inclusion vs. exclusion) neural activations within the dmPFC (BA9), the PCC (BA23), and the precuneus (BA7) were enhanced in BPD even when compared to MD.

title.value: Results of demographic and psychometric measurements in the healthy control (HC), borderline personality disorder (BPD) and major depression (MD) group.

footer.value: BDI, Beck Depression Inventory; BIS, Barratt Impulsiveness Scale; BSL, Borderline Symptom List; HFS, Hurt Feeling Scale; NTS, Need Threat Scale; RSQ, Rejection Sensitivity Questionnaire; numeric scales of “feelings after fMRI” range from 1 (very low) to 4 (very strong); SD, standard deviation; vs., versus; ANOVA, analysis of variance. To control for multiple comparison of the ANOVAs in dependent measures (NTS and feelings after fMRI); a false-discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied significant at p < 0.05 (FDR-corrected) to interfere significant main effects (*). For better demonstrational purposes, we provide measures of effect sizes (Hedges g*) for post hoc comparisons. Please note, positive values of effect sizes reflect higher scores for BPD when comparing HC vs. BPD, and higher scores for MD when comparing HC vs. MD and BPD vs. MD. Moreover, please consider the coding for the NTS-scale: scores range from 1 (very high distress) to 5 (no distress). (+) denotes significant (p < 0.05) differences in post hoc comparisons (Newman Keuls). Readers are reminded that all state measures (NTS and feelings after fMRI) had been taken after the end of the whole cyber-ball paradigm.

value: Effect sizes (Hedge's g*) from post hoc tests

description.value: Demographic, psychometric, and post-fMRI feelings measurements for the HC, BPD, and MD groups, including one-way ANOVA and post hoc effect sizes.

title.value: Significant (p < 0.001, k > 90 Vx corresponding to FWE-correction on cluster level) whole brain group-by-condition interaction effects and post-hoc analyses (p < 0.001, k > 150 Vx corresponding to FWE-correction on cluster level) comparing differential (inclusion vs. passive watching condition) neural activations between groups (HC, healthy controls; BPD, borderline personality disorder; MD, major depression) during the fMRI cyberball paradigm.
